status: research only; product equations, defaults and quality gates unchanged
purpose: Distinguish the collocated product PressureOutlet weak semantics from the previously studied total-stress natural outlet before re-running the original curved Re20 problem.

productBoundaryReading.pressure: PressureOutlet fixes the face static pressure and pressure correction reference.
productBoundaryReading.primaryViscosity: A free outlet velocity has no compact grad(U).n diffusion term.
productBoundaryReading.symmetricCorrection: The symmetric-stress option still applies -nu*grad(U)^T.S using a tangential face gradient.
productBoundaryReading.advection: Outflow retains the transported outlet face velocity; configured backflow handling remains a separate product rule.
productBoundaryReading.consequence: This is not the total-stress condition (2 nu sym(grad U)-pI)n=0 used by the earlier hybrid prototype.

researchImplementation.unknowns: Existing P1 cell/face velocity, P1 static pressure, RT1 compatible load/transport and local 8x8 condensation.
researchImplementation.pressureOutlet: On the open face, subtract the transpose-gradient boundary bilinear form from the full symmetric weak form. This leaves the product's zero primary normal derivative plus retained transpose correction. The manufactured outlet pressure is p=0.
researchImplementation.geometry: Native FvMesh2D square grids; all cells and original faces retained; no threshold or fitted coefficient.
researchImplementation.manufacturedField: u=(4 y (1-y),0), p=8(1-x), nu=1. Inertia vanishes exactly, walls are stationary no-slip, inlet velocity is prescribed, and the right face has p=0 with grad(U).n=0.
researchImplementation.negativeControl: The identical field does not satisfy zero total stress at the outlet because its tangential shear traction is generally nonzero.

nonlinearControl.description: The same manufactured field has zero convective acceleration. The compatible RT1 upwind Navier-Stokes path converged in two Picard solves at n=4,8,16 with the pressure outlet.

fixedPolygonCylinderRe20.geometry: Original Linux fixed 128-segment polygon, 20D outer domain, unchanged coarse/medium FvMesh2D with 4716/17260 cells; nu=0.1, U=1, D=2.
fixedPolygonCylinderRe20.boundary: Left prescribed (1,0), horizontal symmetry, true zero-velocity embedded wall, right product-like p=0 outlet with zero primary normal velocity gradient and retained transpose-gradient symmetric correction.

productVersusNaturalOutlet.interpretation: At the 20D outlet the two boundary conditions perturb this bounded branch only slightly, but they are not algebraically or physically interchangeable.

coarseMediumSpatialChange.interpretation: The compatible formulation removes the old medium-grid high-amplitude branch in this controlled path and gives a modest coarse/medium wall-pressure change, but two levels do not establish asymptotic convergence or qualify local curved-wall pressure.

interpretation.supported: The implemented pressure-outlet weak form reproduces the product boundary decomposition, passes an exact open-flow control, and yields bounded, conservative coarse/medium Re20 solutions on the original fixed-polygon meshes. The prior natural-stress result alone was not evidence for the original product boundary problem.
interpretation.notSupported: The medium result starts from the saved natural-outlet field rather than an independent zero field. Two spatial levels do not qualify local curved-wall pressure; backflow, fine-grid scalability, branch uniqueness and production integration remain open.

build.compiler: g++ Linux, C++20, O2, Wall/Wextra/Wpedantic/Werror; unused-parameter warning suppressed only for the included pre-existing flow_face_test helper
build.nativeCtest: flow_face, flow_boundary, flow_branch_certificate: 3/3 passed; full native/frontend/Electron suites not rerun

failuresRetained: The first edited source did not compile because the new face correction was placed after the face-loop brace.
The second build exposed a local variable name collision with the existing boundary-work accumulator.
Neither failed build produced a runnable binary or accepted numerical field.
